subject.title: Model configuration accepts unvalidated model names, enabling silent misconfiguration

question: Should OpenClaw validate arbitrary configured agent model refs against a trusted/runtime-equivalent catalog as warnings or errors, and should that validation live in `config validate`, doctor, config write/reload, or some combination?
rationale: The source gap is clear, but the durable product choice is whether unknown refs are invalid, warning-only, or allowed for custom and forward-compatible provider setups; automation cannot safely choose that compatibility boundary.

options.title: Add advisory trusted-catalog validation
options.body: Warn in `config validate` and doctor using runtime-equivalent resolution, alias handling, fallback coverage, and catalog-origin awareness without blocking custom/forward-compatible refs by default.

options.title: Hard-fail invalid configured refs
options.body: Reject unresolvable active model refs at config write or startup, preventing runtime surprises but intentionally making previously accepted configs fail earlier.

options.title: Defer to broader model reconciliation
options.body: Keep this issue as a specific repro but only solve it as part of the broader model reconcile/session reset design in https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/28965.

recommendation.title: Add advisory trusted-catalog validation
recommendation.body: Warn in `config validate` and doctor using runtime-equivalent resolution, alias handling, fallback coverage, and catalog-origin awareness without blocking custom/forward-compatible refs by default.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision crosses model selection, config validation, doctor UX, and provider catalog semantics, and steipete has the strongest inspected ownership signal across those paths.
